name: wait_for_joint_arrival
summary: Poll feedback after non-blocking Servo until measured arrival, fault, or wall-clock timeout.

generality.rationale: Applies to any joint-space target and decouples completion checks from simulator world-clock speed.
assumptions: A non-blocking Servo command remains active and joint feedback is readable.
limitations: Does not stop on timeout, verify collision/contact, or establish task success.
tested_tasks: robotwin/press-stapler-aloha-agilex (derived from harness_v2_iter_005; runtime validation pending next run)

level.rationale: Composes repeated atomic arrival verification with wall-clock timeout and stability policy.

composition.strategy: Poll measured joints, require consecutive within-tolerance samples, and terminate on arrival, fault, or wall timeout.

provenance.failure_gap: Blocking Servo timed out because simulator world time lagged wall time; Qwen recovered with block=false but checked contact arrival too early and stopped a valid in-progress command.
evidence: approach block=true world.wait timed out after about 61.6 wall seconds despite a 9.94 world-second trajectory
Qwen then used block=false successfully, but contact was checked after only about 6 wall seconds and failed
